# Independent review: radio required scheduling fc36

The bounded required-setter change is supported for integration, subject to a current-tree source comparison and a separate successor for the 28 radio authored-use source epochs. Candidate `68d2f3450dbe80890f5dfaa2bda90b567e36febf` on `5ddd6f98b9af8c4b4f7bee619eb291c2a9950b1c`, patch SHA256 `3e8830aeb3535bf16729b2c39c14b0383f6c0d667eb686daad482d8afcae7650`. No HTML, CSS or Sass changes occur.

The complete upstream `fc36e668fb72aa4f4798ea5fb09acdbce9c906c4` patch marks a changed radio required property for OnPush checking and removes an upstream test configuration suppressing exhaustive change checks. The tagged 16 legacy setter only coerces and assigns. This candidate retains legacy `BooleanInput` coercion and the existing group-fallback getter, and adds `markForCheck()` after the coerced internal value changes. Identical subsequent coerced values do not mark again. The field initially has value `undefined`, so its first explicit false is a distinct internal transition and can mark despite the same effective native false state; the new test establishes subsequent equal-value suppression, not zero marks for every semantically equivalent initial or group-inherited state. The existing OnPush component is the relevant rendering boundary; this is an intentional scheduling improvement over the reference, not a claim that the reference already performed it.

Verified retained candidate tar SHA256 `2cf96975b6f6adaa83a8bf42f99a756f34bbdd7166ea899120f5605c66f8bffb`, report SHA256 `aba0f8c0f08c78de31e85af283524a3f6e3766a9d4bdb8fcff27e20c3c92cfa8`, 99/99 passed and none skipped, artifact-bound report SHA matches. Independently compared all 512 regular tar members to the extracted test package, with no differences. The retained old tar `4148c2edd526dbac802ddc6f48c620534b2262400f141f072555b2f5396cadfd` also matches all 512 extracted members; its radio source map embeds the exact baseline radio-base SHA256 `e3365e7b338c80cb0b539fb19cb1c8c20d0741f37d4c11f2f46f8620aaec3fbf`. Its direct negative report SHA256 `3d1210ebe98404802c8aaaca7e6c5914f31ed88ed45587705d25350698ee9799` has 96/99: both zoneful and zoneless-provider automatic true-render tests and the coercion/mark-count test fail as intended. That direct report has null artifact hash and the old pack differs from current source elsewhere; it is not a whole-current-product baseline. The retained state records clean candidate source and no source changes during the run.

The automatic-render tests write the public property, await stabilization and inspect native `required` without manual detectChanges, and the targeted spy checks coercion and redundant marks. Zone.js remains loaded during the zoneless-provider test; it is not strict no-Zone coverage. No independent browser replay was performed. This review grants no x64, 21.x, full suite, security or release qualification.
